actions.action: Check the roots for damage or rot
Cut the stem at the marked point or chop off the top/healthy branch
Repot the plant or stump in fresh soil
Root the cuttings directly in soil, optionally with rooting hormone, keeping the soil moist for a couple of weeks
Alternatively, root the cuttings in a glass of water
Move the rooted cutting into a vase with LECA/clay pebbles
Air layer the live stem before chopping and repotting
Repot into a heavy mix with pumice, stone and clay for stability
Add fresh soil to the pot

verdict.reason: The thread mostly blames root rot or death and mentions underwatering only as one commenter's possibility. Repotting appears among many suggestions, but no thorough watering is advised. The dominant chop-and-propagate and root-rot advice would lead to drastic, unnecessary cutting and delay the simple watering fix.
